benchmarks.missing_forecast: a lead the model has no law for is filled by B1 (scoring_protocol.fill_missing)

scoring.scorer: scripts/richer_targets_706.py score_target, unchanged in what it computes (two optional arguments added: the day to drop, further benchmarks)
scoring.score: scoring_protocol.grid_crps on the 23 levels, the mean over leads 1 to 5 per decision day
scoring.interval: scoring_protocol.paired_tests through spread_distribution_634.pair_table: stationary bootstrap, mean block 10, 10000 draws, seed 634, one-sided 95% (the lower bound of the two-sided 90% interval); the pre-onset AUC resamples onsets, 2000 draws, seed 706. Both are #706's

splits.state: the as-of scarcity state of the decision day: ample or scarce

dropped_day_reading: a decision day, as in #805 (scripts/h5_splits_805.py EXCLUDED_DAY): left out of every cut after the benchmarks are built; in the pre-onset AUC the day whose decision day it is is the lead-1 target of the next row
with_column: the scorer run on the same walks with nothing dropped. `score` also runs the scorer with no extra benchmark and refuses unless the B1, B2 and model columns of that run are the 'with' column's, so the added benchmark and argument change no figure

reading.sign_change: a cell whose one-sided 95% lower bound of the skill over a benchmark changes sign when the day is dropped, listed one per line
reading.kill_criterion: any reading against H9's kill criterion (docs/research/hypotheses/H9.md) is a marked question for Eleonora, not a statement of the page. The model reads no calendar column, so the result is provisional and closes no question
